thread:
Emma: Heads up — credential rotation for our out-of-band (BMC) proxy started in eu-west-1 at 09:05 UTC. I'm seeing PXE provisioning spikes and a bunch of BMC session drops on racks r7/r8/r9 (dedicated GPU pool). Raising here so infra knows before this escalates. :warning:
Raj: Looking at logs, provisioning service spitting 401s from bmc-proxy. Do you have the proxy logs?
Emma: Pasting a small snippet from the proxy here:
```
2025-06-12T09:06:12Z bmc-proxy auth error: 401 unauthorized - key mismatch for host rack7-node42
2025-06-12T09:06:15Z provisioner pxe error: client disconnect during tftp transfer
2025-06-12T09:06:30Z bmc-monitor: session closed by remote (credential-change) host=rack8-node03
```
Marcus: How many nodes impacted and what's the capacity hit?
Emma: ~48 servers across 3 racks; ded-gpu-eu1 pool lost ~22% of available GPUs (pod autoscaler already shifting load to us-west).
Jen: Any sign of UEFI/secureboot toggles during these cycles? Secureboot flips cause node reprovision flow to go weird.
Emma: Yes — a handful of machines logged UEFI variable writes during reboot. Example: `secure_boot=0` after BMC reboot. Might be the BMC doing a recovery boot path.
Raj: The rotation job likely invalidated existing BMC sessions which forces controllers to reset. bmc-proxy returned `401: bad-key` for many hosts. The regen job's rollout window overlapped with ongoing provisioning.
deploy-bot: Canary was pushed to 10 racks earlier this week. Rollout policy: linear 1 rack / 5m, auto-rollback=on but rollback triggers only on probe failures (not on external provisioning errors).
Marcus: Okay, do not mass-reboot or reflash. Start rollback and mark affected nodes drained so schedulers don't place GPU workloads on them.
Emma: Manual rollback started: `bmc-cred-regen --undo --region eu-west-1 --batch 0-2` — running now.
Raj: In parallel, increase PXE/tftp timeouts and mark the provisioning probe to skip secureboot validation to allow reboots to complete. Commands:
```
# increase PXE timeout
kubectl -n infra patch configmap pxe-config --patch '{"data":{"tftp_timeout":"30"}}'
# relax secureboot probe for transient recovery
curl -X POST https://provisioner.api/flags --data '{"skip_secureboot_check":true}'
```
Jen: Also, drain the three affected racks in k8s and remove them from the ded-gpu-eu1 rotation to avoid SLOs. I'll notify customer success for any dedicated tenant impact.
Marcus: Runbook action: mark `bmc-rotation` job to add `provisioning_smoke=true` as a canary probe. Current canary only checks auth endpoints, not PXE or cluster provisioning.
Emma: Incident created INC-2025-EUOOB and paging SRE. I'm attaching node lists to the incident. :clipboard:
Raj: Short-term mitigation ideas being executed: session-ttl cache for BMC proxy, soft sessions instead of hard kick during key swap. Long-term: atomic key handoff that preserves existing sessions until clients reauth.
provisioner-bot: Noted: ded-gpu-eu1 autoscaler triggered cross-region burst to us-west to keep capacity. Estimated extra cost ~ $2.3k for 12h.
Marcus: Postmortem TODOs: (1) add auth-failure metric to regen alarms, (2) update canary to include provisioning smoke tests, (3) implement session handoff logic, (4) document secureboot-flap runbook.
Jen: I'll own customer comms and CS notif. Emma/Raj please add timeline and root cause to the incident once rollback completes.
Emma: rollback finished at 09:19 UTC. PXE errors falling back to baseline. Keeping nodes drained for sanity checks for 1h.
Raj: We'll schedule a postmortem meeting and link the runbook edits. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
